s008000.name: Reset: hardware init and main loop
summary: Entered from the emulation-mode RESET vector. Quiets the SNES (IRQ/NMI/DMA/HDMA off, APU ports cleared, force blank),
switches to native 16-bit mode, builds the OAM-clear routine in RAM at $7F8000, uploads the SPC700 engine and samples,
clears RAM and then runs the main loop forever.
Main loop: wait until NMI sets [$10], count a frame in [$13], run the current game mode (GetGameMode), clear [$10], repeat.
Quirk: the RAM routine is generated code: LDA #$F0 followed by 128 STA $0201+4n (every sprite's Y = $F0, off-screen) and an RTL.

SPC700UploadLoop.name: Upload data blocks to SPC700
summary: Sends one or more blocks to the SPC700 through APU ports $2140-$2143 using the IPL boot ROM transfer protocol.
Block format at [$00]: 16-bit length, 16-bit SPC700 destination address, then the data bytes. A block of length 0 ends the
transfer; its address is where the SPC700 starts running.
Parameters: [$00]-[$02]: 24-bit ROM address of the first block.
Returns: APU ports cleared; processor flags preserved.

UploadSPCEngine.name: Upload SPC700 engine
summary: Points [$00] at $0E:8000 (SPC700 engine and its initial data) and falls through into UploadDataToSPC.

UploadDataToSPC.name: Upload data with IRQs disabled
summary: Wraps SPC700UploadLoop in SEI/CLI because the handshake is timing sensitive.
Parameters: [$00]-[$02]: 24-bit ROM address of the data. Note: always leaves IRQs enabled (CLI).

UploadSamples.name: Upload sample data to SPC700
summary: Points [$00] at $0F:8000 (BRR sample pointers and data) and uploads it via StrtSPCMscUpld.

UploadMusicBank1.name: Upload music bank 1 (title, overworld)
summary: Points [$00] at $0E:98B1 and falls through into StrtSPCMscUpld. Called when the title screen and the overworld are loaded.

StrtSPCMscUpld.name: Request and run SPC700 upload
summary: Common tail of the sample and music uploads. Writes $FF to APU port 1 (probably asks the running SPC700 engine to jump back
to its IPL loader), uploads the blocks at [$00], then falls into SPC700ZeroLoop to clear the ports.
Parameters: [$00]-[$02]: 24-bit ROM address of the data.

SPC700ZeroLoop.name: Clear APU ports and sound mirrors
summary: Clears APU I/O ports $2140-$2143 and the RAM mirrors $1DF9-$1E00 (sound requests and last-sent music value $1DFF).
$008134 (entry point from the Mario Start game mode): uploads the level music bank only when [$1425] is non-zero, [$0109] = $E9,
or [$0109], [$141A] and [$141D] are all zero; otherwise returns without uploading.

UploadMusicBank2.name: Upload music bank 2 (levels)
summary: Points [$00] at $0E:AED6 (level music) and jumps to StrtSPCMscUpld.

UploadMusicBank3.name: Upload music bank 3 (ending)
summary: Points [$00] at $03:E400 (ending/credits music) and jumps to StrtSPCMscUpld.

NMIStart.name: NMI handler: sound, PPU mirrors, DMA
summary: Runs once per frame at the start of V-blank. Saves registers, delivers queued music/SFX requests to the SPC700, forces blank,
copies the window/color-math mirrors [$41]-[$44] to the PPU, then does all VRAM/CGRAM/OAM DMA and reads the controllers.
Lag detection: [$10] is cleared by the main loop when it finishes a frame. If [$10] is still non-zero on entry the game logic
overran the frame (lag), so the heavy DMA work is skipped and only scroll registers are updated.
[$0D9B] (special level mode): bit 7 set sends control to the Mode 7 boss room path at $0082C4. Falls into NMINotSpecialLv.

NMINotSpecialLv.name: NMI tail: scroll, IRQ setup, Mode 7 path
summary: $008246: writes BG1 and BG2 scroll from the RAM mirrors, then (normal levels) arms the status bar IRQ at $008292, zeroes BG3 scroll,
restores brightness [$0DAE] and HDMA enable [$0D9F] and returns with RTI.
$0082C4: NMI path for Mode 7 boss rooms ([$0D9B] bit 7): same DMA work, then Mode 7 center and matrix registers from [$2A]-[$35].
$00835C: chooses the IRQ scanline for those rooms ($24, or $2D for some bosses).

IRQHandler.name: IRQ vector entry
summary: Masks further IRQs and falls into IRQStart.

IRQStart.name: IRQ: save registers, check timer
summary: Saves state, acknowledges the IRQ via $4211 and ignores it unless the V-count timer fired. Bit 7 of [$0D9B] set sends control
to the Mode 7 boss room IRQ code at $0083BA. Otherwise falls into IRQNMIEnding.

IRQNMIEnding.name: IRQ: set BG3 scroll and screen mode
summary: Status bar raster split. Writes NMITIMEN from A, waits for H-blank, then sets BG3 scroll from [$22]-[$25], BGMODE from [$3E]
and CGADSUB from [$40] for the part of the screen below the status bar. Restores registers and falls into the RTI.
Parameters: A = value for NMITIMEN ($4200).

EmptyHandler.name: IRQ return and Mode 7 boss splits
summary: $0083B9: the RTI that ends every IRQ.
$0083BA: IRQ path for Mode 7 boss rooms. Iggy/Larry ([$0D9B] bit 6 clear) use a single split that switches to Mode 7 below the
status bar. Others use two stages counted in [$11]: stage 0 programs a second V-count IRQ at line $AE - [$1888] and enters Mode 7;
stage 1 restores the Mode 1 layer 1 settings below it.

SETL1SCROLL.name: Set BG1 base addresses and scroll
summary: Sets BG1 tilemap to VRAM $5800 (64x32), BG1 tiles to VRAM $7000, and BG1 scroll to [$1A]/[$1B] horizontally and
[$1C] + [$1888] / [$1D] vertically. Used by the Mode 7 boss room code to restore Mode 1 BG1 around the Mode 7 region.
$008439 (last line here) is the Y = $20 entry point of WaitForHBlank.

WaitForHBlank.name: Wait for H-blank, then delay
summary: Polls HVBJOY ($4212) bit 6. If already in H-blank, retries with Y = $20 (overwriting Y); once H-blank begins, burns Y loop
iterations (DEY/BNE, 5 cycles each) so the caller's PPU writes land at a consistent point in the scanline.
Parameters: Y: delay loop count (entry at $008439 uses $20).

DoSomeSpriteDMA.name: DMA OAM buffer to OAM
summary: Copies the $0220-byte OAM shadow buffer at $00:0200 to OAM using DMA channel 0, then sets OAM address to [$3F]
with priority rotation on, so the sprite at that index has highest priority.

s008475.name: Table: OAM size table offsets
summary: Offsets into the $0420 table for CODE_008494: 8 per step, read with an 8-bit index Y = 0,2,4..$1E. Odd bytes are zero padding.

s008494.name: Pack OAM size bits into high table
summary: Packs the one-byte-per-sprite size/X-high table at $0420-$049F (values 0-3) into the 2-bits-per-sprite OAM high table at
$0400-$041F: byte = s3<<6 | s2<<4 | s1<<2 | s0, four sprites per byte. 16 iterations of two output bytes each.
$0084C8: long-call wrapper (RTL) that sets the data bank to $00 and runs LoadScrnImage; called from bank $0C.

ImagePointers.name: Pointer table: stripe images
summary: 3-byte pointers (16-bit address, bank), indexed by [$12] (byte offset = image number * 3). Each points to a stripe image: a list
of VRAM upload records read by LoadScrnImage. Entry $00 is the runtime buffer at $7F:837D that the game fills itself.
Cutscene text numbering is inferred from the pointer order (each text line is $35 bytes after the next).

LoadScrnImage.name: Upload stripe image to VRAM
summary: Loads the 24-bit pointer for image [$12] from ImagePointers into [$00] and uploads it with CODE_00871E. Runs every NMI.
If [$12] = 0 (the RAM buffer at $7F:837D) the buffer is emptied afterwards: write index $7F:837B = 0, first byte = $FF.
[$12] is cleared so that an image is only loaded once.
Image record format (parsed by CODE_00871E): VRAM address high, low, then a word (bit 7 = vertical increment, bit 6 = RLE, low
14 bits = byte count - 1), then the data. A record whose first byte has bit 7 set ends the image.
$0085FA (separate routine, called at the start of most game modes): turns off NMI/IRQ/HDMA and the screen (TurnOffIO), fills the
BG3 tilemap (VRAM $5000-$5FFF) with tile $FC / attributes $38, hides all sprites via $7F8000 and DMAs OAM.

s008649.name: Table: DMA setup for BG3 clear
summary: 7 bytes copied to $4310-$4316: DMAP $08 (fixed source, 1 register), B-bus $18, source $00:0000, size $1000.
